summary.intent: Implement two new test packages — SDK-driven E2E tests (`tests/sdk-e2e/`) and SDK-driven load tests (`tests/load/`) — as described in a pre-approved implementation plan, then open a PR.
summary.outcome: All 5 implementation phases completed: 10 E2E test suites, 5 load scenarios, 3 workload definitions, full harness infrastructure, and 2 CI workflows created. Both packages compile cleanly with zero TypeScript errors.

repo: `setApiClientConfig` in `packages/api-client/src/instance.ts` is a module-level singleton — multi-account tests must run serially, switching the config between accounts before each operation.
The `POST /auth/test-login` endpoint is the CI auth bypass pattern used across all test types — returns `{ accessToken, refreshToken, isNewUser, publicKeyHex, privateKeyHex }`.
Internal SDK state (`folderTree`, `binState`) is accessible via `(client as any).folderTree.get(ipnsName)` for in-memory verification without a full IPNS round-trip.
The existing Playwright load test drives ~70 ops/client across 10 concurrent browser contexts; translating this to SDK removes browser overhead and enables much higher concurrency.
Release Please config uses `extra-files` to track version bumps in non-standard package locations — new test packages must be added there.

CipherBoxClient emits typed `SdkEvent` lifecycle events (`operation:start`, `operation:end`, `error`, `folder:loaded`, `folder:updated`, etc.) via `client.on()` — usable for load test metrics collection.
The workspace has three groups in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: `apps/*`, `packages/*`, `tests/*` — new test packages go under `tests/`.
k6 was ruled out for load testing because its Go-based JS runtime lacks Node.js crypto support needed by `@noble/*` and `eciesjs`.

code.finding: Gold-standard test setup pattern: test-login → initializeVault → encryptVaultKeys → setApiClientConfig → new CipherBoxClient → registerFolder. Extracted verbatim into test-harness.ts.
Singleton config with shared `_refreshPromise` to prevent concurrent 401 refresh races — all sdk-core IPNS functions use this implicitly, making it the key constraint for multi-account test design.
Full operation surface: folder CRUD, upload/download with progress, bin lifecycle, share/revoke, internal `withOperation()` wrapper that emits typed events with start/end/error lifecycle.

workflow: TypeScript `noUnusedLocals` strict mode caused several post-write edit cycles to remove unused imports — better to check this incrementally rather than after all files are written.
Running `pnpm install` at root after adding new workspace packages updates the lockfile and wires workspace protocol dependencies in a single step.

The exploration sub-agent was launched before implementation files were written, but its results arrived after the implementation was already complete — for well-scoped tasks with sufficient prior context, the agent added latency without contributing new information.

friction: Multiple edit cycles needed after initial file writes due to `noUnusedLocals` TypeScript errors — unused imports introduced during copy-paste-and-adapt from reference files.
Some Edit tool calls failed silently (string already matched what was in the file from the Write call) requiring re-reads to confirm state.
The background exploration sub-agent completed after the implementation was already done, providing no value and consuming context.
open_items: SDK E2E and load tests have not been run against a live environment — full validation requires local API + IPFS stack.
The `sdk-e2e.yml` CI workflow starts the API with `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api start:prod` — this script reference was not verified to exist in the API package.
Share/invite test suites use raw API calls rather than SDK methods where SDK equivalents may not yet exist — these may need updating as SDK coverage expands.

Load test scenarios use configurable env vars (`LOAD_TEST_CLIENTS`, `LOAD_TEST_DURATION`) but no baseline performance thresholds are encoded — p95/p99 assertions could be added once baseline numbers are established.
The `tests/load/` package is not added to the root `pnpm test` script or any automatic CI trigger — it's manual-dispatch only by design, but should be documented in the project README.
